body.text:
[Warm, conversational voice, measured delivery] A tech lead presented a new direction for a prototype and walked the team through the features to build. [brief pause, about a quarter of a second] In the meetings that followed, she explained the architecture and how the modules connected.

[pause, about half a second]

[Calm, clear storytelling voice] With the design explained and user stories ready to pick up, she expected implementation to begin. [brief pause, about a quarter of a second] But the stories named features without making the expected output clear.

[pause, about half a second]

[Calm, clear storytelling voice] The developers researched the technologies and explored examples to work out what would fit. [brief pause, about a quarter of a second] Each possibility raised more questions. [brief pause, about a quarter of a second] The research expanded into features and approaches the prototype did not need.

[pause, about half a second]

[Calm, clear storytelling voice] At the next catch-up, the team had plenty to share about the technology, but very little working software to show.

[pause, about half a second]

[Calm, clear storytelling voice] The lead had treated explaining the direction as completing the communication. [brief pause, about a quarter of a second] But the developers needed the priority again, when they had a concrete piece of work in front of them.

[pause, about half a second]

[Calm, clear storytelling voice] People do not bring every question they will need answered to a presentation. [brief pause, about a quarter of a second] Some questions appear when they apply what they heard. [brief pause, about a quarter of a second] Knowing how modules connect does not tell you how far to take a feature, or which possibilities to ignore.

[pause, about half a second]

[Calm, clear storytelling voice] Repeat the priority where those decisions happen. [brief pause, about a quarter of a second] The user stories were another chance to state what the prototype needed. [brief pause, about a quarter of a second] Make the expected output clear, including how far to take the feature and what to leave out.

[pause, about half a second]

[Calm, clear storytelling voice] Saying it once is not the finish line. [brief pause, about a quarter of a second] If the team fills the gaps with its own interpretation, you will have more work to course-correct later. [brief pause, about a quarter of a second] Keep repeating the priority until it appears in what the team is doing.

[pause, about half a second]

[Softening, reflective] Worry less about sounding repetitive, and more about whether the priority is guiding the work.
